metaDescription: Six wall mounted reading lamps compared on mounting, dimming, beam angle and USB charging, for readers who want a clear nightstand and focused light.
introParagraphs: A wall mounted reading lamp frees up the nightstand and puts the light right where your book is, and for many readers it is the neatest answer to a crowded bedside. This guide compares six wall and headboard lamps: the WisHomee plug-in lamp with a 5V/2A USB port, the SANKEDOU touch lamp with two timers, the GOODATE swing arm sconce, the LiFMIRA with a half hour auto-off, the Adust with a 60 degree beam and the LEDSONLINE with a tight 25 degree focus.

These lamps differ in more than looks. Beam angles run from 25 degrees on the LEDSONLINE to 60 degrees on the Adust and LiFMIRA, colour options span a single 6000K white on the LEDSONLINE to three selectable tones on the WisHomee, and only some add USB charging. Some plug into a standard outlet with a cord, like the GOODATE with its 6 foot cord, while others are designed for fixed installation, which changes who can fit them without an electrician.

We evaluated each lamp from product specs and buyer feedback, weighing how easy it is to install, how focused the beam is, how simple the controls are in the dark and whether it suits a headboard or a wall. Older eyes need more light than younger ones and are more sensitive to glare, so lamps with dimming and a directional beam that keeps light off the pillow ranked higher.

products.name: WisHomee Plug-In Wall Mounted Reading Light with USB
products.description:
The WisHomee is the most practical wall lamp here because it avoids wiring altogether. It plugs into an outlet, uses a gooseneck that adjusts 360 degrees, and mounts to a wall, a plank or a headboard. Three colour temperatures, 3000K warm, 4000K neutral and 6000K white, are selectable, and a long press adjusts brightness while a light touch changes mode.

It also carries a 5V/2A USB port at the lamp base, which charges a phone without needing a nightstand charger. The tradeoff is that the touch logic of long press for brightness and light touch for colour takes practice, and the cord has to be hidden or run to an outlet. It is mid-priced in this lineup.

Installation takes a few screws and a visible cord, and the gooseneck can be wiped clean. Compared with the SANKEDOU, which adds timers, the WisHomee offers more colour choice and faster charging. It suits the reader who wants flexibility without a trip to an electrician.
products.bestFor: Readers who want plug-in simplicity, colour choice and phone charging
pros: Plug-in design needs no wiring
Three colour temperatures from 3000K to 6000K
5V/2A USB port charges a phone
Mounts to a wall, plank or headboard
cons: Press logic for brightness and colour takes practice
Cord needs managing along the wall

products.name: SANKEDOU LED Wall Mounted Reading Light with Touch Control
products.description:
The SANKEDOU is a focused touch lamp that lights the book while keeping the rest of the room dark. It has five dimming levels, two timer functions that help if you fall asleep reading, and a USB output at the lamp. A 360 degree gooseneck lets you aim it at the page.

The benefit is the timers, which switch the lamp off automatically and save energy. The tradeoff is that five dimming levels is coarser than a stepless control, and a touch panel mounted on a wall can be harder to find in the dark than a physical switch. Mounting also requires fixing it to the wall or headboard.

It is a straightforward lamp to live with and wipes clean easily. Against the LiFMIRA, which has one half hour timer, the SANKEDOU gives more timer choice and more dimming steps. It is a sensible pick for readers who nod off with the light on.
products.bestFor: Readers who fall asleep with the light on
pros: Two timer settings switch off automatically
Five dimming levels for evening use
Focused beam keeps the room dark
USB output charges a device
cons: Five steps are coarser than stepless dimming
Wall mounted touch panel is harder to find in the dark

products.name: GOODATE Plug-In Swing Arm Wall Sconce
products.description:
The GOODATE is a traditional swing arm sconce in black metal that looks like furniture rather than a gadget. It has a stepless dimmer switch, a swing arm that adjusts 270 degrees up and down, and a 6 foot plug-in cord, although it can also be hardwired. The dimmer gives exact brightness control rather than steps.

Its tradeoff is that it is a fixture rather than a compact book light, so it takes more wall space and the plug-in cord is visible. Its design also leans toward ambient light more than a tight beam, so it is less focused than the LEDSONLINE. Hardwiring needs an electrician in most homes.

Setup is easy in plug-in mode and the smooth switch is simple to use. Compared with the WisHomee, it offers true stepless dimming and a more decorative look, though it has no USB charging.
products.bestFor: Readers who want stepless dimming and a decorative fixture
pros: Stepless dimmer switch gives exact brightness
Swing arm adjusts 270 degrees
Plug-in or hardwired installation
Black metal looks like a real fixture
cons: Bulkier than a compact book light
Visible cord in plug-in mode and no USB port

products.name: LiFMIRA Wall Mounted LED Bedside Reading Light
products.description:
The LiFMIRA is the lowest cost wall lamp here and still offers a useful feature set. It uses 14 SMD2835 LEDs with adjustable colour from 3000K to 6000K, a 60 degree beam, a 360 degree gooseneck and a USB charging port. A half hour auto-off timer turns it off if you drift to sleep.

The tradeoff is that 14 LEDs and a small head give less raw light than a bigger fixture, so very dense print may need a stronger lamp. The timer is a single fixed setting rather than selectable. It is a slim headboard lamp, so it saves space.

It mounts easily and the neck wipes clean. Against the Adust, it adds a USB port and colour choice for less money, which makes it a good first wall lamp.
products.bestFor: Budget shoppers who want a slim headboard lamp with USB
pros: USB charging port on the lamp
Colour adjustable from 3000K to 6000K
Half hour auto-off prevents all-night light

products.name: Adust Bedside Wall Reading Light
products.description:
The Adust is a minimalist headboard reading lamp with a narrow 60 degree beam. Its 13 inch flexible gooseneck lets you aim light at a page, and a silent touch button turns it on or off and adjusts brightness. The focused beam keeps light off your partner.

The tradeoff is that its 3W output is modest, so it works best at close range, and a single touch button must handle every function. It has no USB port and no stated colour range. It is the most expensive of the compact lamps, which is hard to justify against the LiFMIRA.

It is easy to install on a headboard and wipes clean. In this comparison it is for people who want a simple directional lamp without extras.
products.bestFor: Readers who want a simple, directional headboard light
pros: Narrow beam keeps light on the book
13 inch gooseneck aims easily
Silent touch button avoids clicks
Compact profile saves space
cons: 3W output is modest for dense print
No USB port or colour choice

products.name: LEDSONLINE Wall Mounted Bed Reading Lamp
products.description:
The LEDSONLINE has the tightest beam of any lamp here at 25 degrees, with a 6000K pure white light. A wide voltage AC85-265V driver supports consistent, flicker-free light, and a reinforced 285mm metal core neck with a silicone sleeve adjusts silently and holds position.

The tradeoff is that a 6000K white with a narrow beam can feel stark for bedtime, and there is no dimming or warm option listed. The listing also notes it is designed for standard wall installation, so confirm how it connects before buying. It is the least flexible lamp in the group for colour.

The silicone neck wipes clean and holds firm. Compared with the Adust's 60 degrees, it is more focused but offers fewer features. It suits readers who want a tight spotlight.
products.bestFor: Readers who want a very tight, bright spotlight on the page
pros: 25 degree beam focuses light on the page
Metal core neck holds position silently
Wide voltage driver for stable light
Strong 6000K white for contrast
cons: No dimming or warm option listed

buyingCriteria.explanation: Hardwired lamps need an electrician in most homes, while plug-in lamps need only an outlet and a visible cord. The WisHomee plugs in, the GOODATE offers a 6 foot cord or hardwiring, and the LEDSONLINE lists a wide AC85-265V driver and is designed for standard wall installation. A renter should favour plug-in models. Check the cord length against the distance to your outlet and plan to hide it with a channel.

A narrow beam keeps light on the page and off a sleeping partner. The LEDSONLINE focuses at 25 degrees, the Adust and LiFMIRA at 60 degrees, and the GOODATE casts a broader fixture light. A tight beam suits close reading but can leave edges of the page dim. Match the beam to how far the lamp sits from your book.

Older eyes need much more light than younger ones for fine detail, with AARP and Rensselaer guidance suggesting about 1,000 lux on the task. The GOODATE's stepless dimmer, the SANKEDOU's five levels and the WisHomee's three colour temperatures each handle this differently. Warmer light is gentler near bedtime and cooler light adds contrast. Choose a lamp that dims and offers at least one warm setting.

A wall lamp must reach your book from where it is fixed. The Adust's 13 inch gooseneck and the LEDSONLINE's 285mm neck set the reach, while the GOODATE's swing arm adjusts 270 degrees. Mount it above and slightly beside your pillow so the light falls on the page rather than your face. Test the height with a book in hand before drilling.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Controls you can reach lying down
buyingCriteria.explanation: A switch on a wall lamp must be found in the dark. The GOODATE has an on/off dimmer switch, the SANKEDOU and Adust use touch controls, and the WisHomee uses press logic that takes practice. Physical switches are easier for stiff fingers than a touch zone. Choose controls within easy reach of your pillow.

A wall lamp can also charge a phone and switch itself off. The WisHomee offers a 5V/2A USB port, the SANKEDOU offers two timers, and the LiFMIRA gives a half hour auto-off with a USB port. A timer is valuable if you doze off, and higher amperage charges faster. Decide which of these features you will use before paying for it.

howWeEvaluated.title: Installation ease
howWeEvaluated.description: The WisHomee and GOODATE offer plug-in, which scored well, while the LEDSONLINE's installation needs checking. Easier installation scored higher for renters.

howWeEvaluated.title: Beam and light quality
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at beam angle, colour range and dimming. The LEDSONLINE's 25 degree beam is the tightest, the WisHomee gives three colours, and the GOODATE offers stepless dimming. Directional light with dimming scored highest.

howWeEvaluated.title: Controls
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered switches, touch panels and press logic. The GOODATE's switch scored best for simplicity, while the WisHomee's press logic scored lower. Controls reachable from a pillow gained points.

howWeEvaluated.title: Charging and timers
howWeEvaluated.description: We counted USB ports and timers. The WisHomee's 5V/2A port and the SANKEDOU's two timers stand out, and the Adust and LEDSONLINE have neither. Useful extras scored higher.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value
howWeEvaluated.description: The LiFMIRA is the lowest cost and the LEDSONLINE the highest. We favoured lamps whose features justified their rank.

cards.label: Narrow beam
cards.text: The LEDSONLINE at 25 degrees puts light only on the page. Choose it for close reading in a shared bed.

cards.label: Wide beam
cards.text: The Adust and LiFMIRA at 60 degrees, and the GOODATE sconce, light a larger area. Choose them for magazines and general reading.

howToChoose.note: Recommendation: the LEDSONLINE for tight focus and the GOODATE for broad comfort.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A gooseneck you can aim, a control within reach of the pillow and a dimmer so you can lower the light as you tire.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The WisHomee's gooseneck and USB port suit lying down, and the SANKEDOU's timers help if you doze.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want stepless dimming and a real fixture look, as with the GOODATE. Spend more for the WisHomee if you want charging and colour choice.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You want a simple headboard light, where the LiFMIRA covers the basics. Save if you read only occasionally.

faq.q: How do I choose between a plug-in and hardwired wall lamp?
faq.a: A plug-in lamp like the WisHomee needs only an outlet and a visible cord. A hardwired lamp looks cleaner but needs an electrician. If you rent or want an easy install, choose plug-in.

faq.q: How high should I mount a reading lamp?
faq.a: Mount it above and slightly beside the pillow so light falls on the page rather than your face. Test the position with a book before drilling. A gooseneck like the Adust's 13 inch neck allows fine adjustment.

faq.q: Is a narrow beam better for reading?
faq.a: A narrow beam like the LEDSONLINE's 25 degrees keeps light on the page and off a partner. It can leave page edges dim. A wider 60 degree beam suits magazines.

faq.q: Can these lamps charge my phone?
faq.a: The WisHomee offers a 5V/2A USB port, and the SANKEDOU and LiFMIRA also include USB output. Higher amperage charges faster. The GOODATE, Adust and LEDSONLINE do not charge devices.
A timer turns the lamp off if you fall asleep. The SANKEDOU offers two timers and the LiFMIRA a half hour auto-off. They are useful and save energy.

faq.q: How do I hide the cord?
faq.a: Use a paintable cord channel along the wall to the outlet. Keep the cord away from the bed edge. The GOODATE's 6 foot cord gives some reach.
